title: The LORD Rejects Dishonorable Sacrifices
summary_text: The LORD answers Israel's doubts by declaring love for Jacob and hatred for Esau. Edom may try to rebuild, but He will destroy its work and show His greatness beyond Israel. The priests dishonor Him by bringing blind, sick, lame, and stolen animals to His altar. He rejects their offerings and says His name will be great among the nations, who will bring pure offerings. As the great King, He curses anyone who vows a sound animal but sacrifices a defective one.
key_points: The LORD declares love for Jacob and hatred for Esau, and calls Edom the Land of Wickedness under His judgment.
The priests despise God's name by placing defective animals on His altar, offerings unfit even for their governor.
The LORD would rather have the temple doors shut than accept useless altar fires, while His name will be great among nations.
God rejects contemptuous worship and curses the deceiver who promises an acceptable animal but sacrifices a defective one.

title: Priests and Judah Break Their Covenants
summary_text: The LORD threatens priests with a curse and shame for breaking His covenant with Levi. Unlike Levi's true teaching, theirs leads people astray and shows favor to some over others. Malachi also accuses Judah of breaking faith by marrying the daughter of a foreign god. God rejects offerings because men betray their wives; He seeks godly children and says He hates divorce. The people weary Him by calling evil good in His sight and questioning His justice.
key_points: The LORD's commandment warns that He will curse the priests' blessings and humiliate them for failing to honor His name.
Levi's covenant brought life, peace, and teaching that turned people from iniquity, but the priests violate it through false instruction and partiality in law.
Malachi condemns Judah's broken faith and marriage to the daughter of a foreign god as profaning the sanctuary.
God rejects offerings brought to His altar by men betraying their wives and tells them to guard their spirit against breaking faith.
The people weary God by calling evildoers pleasing to Him and questioning where His justice is.

title: The LORD Comes to Refine and Judge
summary_text: The LORD will send a messenger to prepare His way, and the Lord will come to His temple as the Messenger of the covenant. Like fire and soap, He will purify Levi's sons for offerings in righteousness and judge evil and oppression. He calls His people to return by bringing the full tithe, promising blessing and fruitful land. Some say serving God is useless, but He hears those who fear Him and records their names. He will spare them as His own, making the difference clear between the righteous and wicked.
key_points: The Messenger of the covenant will come to the temple and refine Levi's sons so their offerings please the LORD.
The LORD promises judgment against sorcerers, adulterers, liars, and those who exploit workers, widows, orphans, and foreigners.
The unchanging LORD calls Jacob's descendants to return, declaring them under a curse for robbing Him in tithes and offerings.
God invites the people to bring the full tithe and promises generous blessing and fruitful land.
God hears those who fear Him despite others' harsh words and promises to distinguish His servants from the wicked.

title: The Coming Day and Elijah's Return
summary_text: The LORD announces a coming day that will burn up the arrogant and wicked, while those who fear Him receive healing from the sun of righteousness and leap with joy. He commands Israel to remember the law He gave Moses at Horeb. Before His great Day, He will send Elijah the prophet to turn fathers and children toward each other, lest He strike the land with a curse.
key_points: The wicked will burn like stubble, while those fearing the LORD receive healing and trample the wicked as ashes.
The LORD commands Israel to remember Moses' law, given at Horeb for the whole people.
Elijah will turn fathers and children toward each other before the LORD's Day, averting the threatened curse.
